public.title: Workshop FAQ accordion
public.description:
Build an accessible accordion for a community workshop FAQ. The starter provides three questions and their answers. Add the interaction in your selected framework while keeping the content and question order intact.

All answers begin collapsed. Activating a question toggles only its own answer. Multiple answers may be open at the same time, and activating an open question closes it without changing the others. Keep each question a native button inside a level-two heading.

Use aria-expanded on every question button and aria-controls pointing to its answer. Each answer must be a region labelled by its question button and use the hidden attribute while collapsed. Preserve a visible keyboard focus indicator. Tab moves through the question buttons in document order; Enter and Space activate the focused button. Arrow-key navigation is outside this exercise.

You assess this exercise yourself. A preview that renders is not proof that the requirements work. Use the manual checklist before choosing Mark complete.
hints: A native button already supports Enter and Space. Handle its activation rather than replacing the button with a clickable div.
Store whether each question is open, then derive both aria-expanded and the answer visibility from that state.
Toggle one question without clearing the state for other questions. In reactive frameworks, create a new array or update a reactive value so the view refreshes.
checklist: On initial load all three answers are hidden and every question has aria-expanded set to false.
Activate the first question: its answer becomes visible and its aria-expanded becomes true. Activate it again: both return to the collapsed state.
Open the first and second questions. Both answers stay open. Close the first; the second stays open. Repeat with the third question.
Use only the keyboard: Tab through all question buttons in order and see a clear focus indicator. Enter and Space each toggle the focused answer once without moving focus.

Inspect the rendered elements: each native button is inside a level-two heading, has a unique id and aria-controls matching its answer; each answer is a labelled region and has the hidden attribute exactly when collapsed.
Check every question after repeated open/close actions. The displayed content stays in order, and aria-expanded always matches whether its answer is visible.

Workshop questions

Open any questions you need. More than one answer may stay open.

Bring a water bottle, a pencil, and a notebook. We supply the tools for the workshop.

The studio opens at 09:30. The first workshop begins at 10:00.

The main entrance and all workshop rooms are on the ground floor. Contact the host if you need other arrangements.

`; // TODO: Toggle only the activated question. Keep aria-expanded and hidden in sync.

Workshop questions

Open any questions you need. More than one answer may stay open.

{#each questions as question (question.id)}

{question.answer}

svelte-javascript.App.svelte:
Workshop questions

Open any questions you need. More than one answer may stay open.

{#each questions as question (question.id)}

{question.answer}

{/each}

explanation:
Maintain a set of open question identifiers. When one question is activated, remove its identifier if present or add it if absent. Do not replace the entire set with only the most recently activated question: this accordion allows multiple open answers.

The Vanilla JS reference reads the current aria-expanded value, updates it, and sets the associated panel hidden property to the prior expanded state. React derives the view from a state array with a functional update. Vue uses a reactive array. Svelte assigns a replacement array so the template updates.

Native buttons supply Enter and Space activation and stay in the tab order. Stable unique button and panel identifiers connect aria-controls and aria-labelledby. Every render derives aria-expanded and hidden from the same open state. No custom key handler is needed, so a single keyboard activation cannot trigger both a key handler and a click handler.

The references demonstrate one solution for each framework. Use the checklist to inspect your own implementation; this exercise does not run automatic grading.
